# contentful_app_definition (Resource)

Manages a Contentful App Definition: the app's name, hosting source, locations in the web app, and parameter definitions. Use `contentful_app_installation` to install it in an environment.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Deploy the app separately and replace src with its HTTPS URL.
resource "contentful_app_definition" "this" {
  organization_id = var.contentful_organization_id

  name = "Editorial tools"
  src  = "https://app.example.com"

  locations = [
    { location = "app-config" },
    {
      location = "entry-field"
      field_types = [
        { type = "Symbol" },
        { type = "Link", link_type = "Entry" },
        { type = "Array", items = { type = "Symbol" } },
        { type = "Array", items = { type = "Link", link_type = "Asset" } },
      ]
    },
    {
      location        = "page"
      navigation_item = { name = "Editorial tools", path = "/editorial-tools" }
    },
  ]

  parameters = {
    installation = [
      {
        id      = "refreshInterval"
        name    = "Refresh interval"
        type    = "Number"
        default = jsonencode(42)
      },
      {
        id      = "enabled"
        name    = "Enabled"
        type    = "Boolean"
        default = jsonencode(false)
      },
      {
        id      = "theme"
        name    = "Theme"
        type    = "Enum"
        options = [jsonencode({ light = "Light" }), jsonencode("dark")]
        default = jsonencode("light")
      },
      {
        id   = "accessToken"
        name = "Access Token"
        type = "Secret"
      },
    ]
  }
}
```

## Field types

An `entry-field` location declares which field types the app can edit. This does
not create content fields or select the app as their editor.

Contentful validates field types and link targets. Array item types are not
interchangeable with outer field types; for example, use `Symbol` or `Link` for
array items. The provider accepts `ResourceLink` definitions with `link_type`
following the Contentful SDK's structure, but successful App Definition API
support for these forms has not been established.

Exact repeated simple `app-config` locations and repeated complete Symbol or
Array-of-Symbol field definitions are rejected before writing. Distinct Link targets
remain distinct; these checks do not impose a general location/type uniqueness rule.

## Parameter values

Use `jsonencode` to distinguish JSON types: `jsonencode(42)` is a number,
`jsonencode("42")` is a string, and `jsonencode(false)` is a Boolean. For Symbol,
Number, Boolean, Enum, and Secret declarations, defaults must encode one of these
primitive types. The provider preserves that type without requiring it to match the
declaration's `type` or an Enum option. Omit `default` to leave it unspecified;
`jsonencode(null)` is rejected.

Options may be omitted, including for Enum, or configured on other parameter types.
For these known types, a configured list must be nonempty, and each option must be a
nonempty JSON string or a single-member object, such as `jsonencode({light = "Light"})`.
Mixed string/object options, repeated values, and non-string object values are permitted.
Unknown future parameter types remain service-validated.

Secret declarations are permitted in both installation and instance scope. This does
not establish secrecy or redaction guarantees for installed instance values. Do not
put real secrets in declaration defaults.

## Validation limits

Validation catches known invalid shapes when their values are available. Values derived
from other resources may remain unknown until apply. Use the documented snake_case
attribute names: Terraform can discard misspelled keys inside nested objects before
the provider receives them, so validation cannot detect every typo.

## Updating existing definitions

Reads and imports preserve existing location and parameter values, including values that would
be invalid in a new request. Updates validate the complete planned locations and parameters,
including values retained by `ignore_changes`. An unrelated update can therefore
plan successfully and fail during apply before this definition is written to
Contentful. Other resources in the apply may already have changed.

Correct invalid values before updating the definition. If those attributes are
ignored, remove the relevant `ignore_changes` rule to apply the correction.
Configuration must still be valid, including when destroying the resource. If a
configuration error blocks destroy, correct the configuration and retry destroy;
that correction does not first need to be applied to Contentful.

## Schema

### Required

- `locations` (Attributes List) Locations where the app can be rendered in the Contentful web app. Use `[]` for no locations. Rendering locations require a frontend hosting source. When the provider sends a `src` URL, including one retained from state, Contentful requires at least one location other than `dialog`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--locations))
- `name` (String) A human-readable name of the app.
- `organization_id` (String) ID of the organization that owns the app definition. Changing this value replaces the resource.

### Optional

- `bundle_id` (String) ID of the App Bundle when the app is hosted on Contentful.
- `parameters` (Attributes) Definitions of configuration parameters. At most eight instance declarations are supported. For known parameter types, defaults encode a JSON string, number, or Boolean independently of the declared type; configured options are nonempty lists of nonempty JSON strings or single-member JSON objects. Options may be omitted, and Enum default membership is not enforced. Unknown future parameter types remain service-validated. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--parameters))
- `src` (String) Public URL of the app. Must be non-empty and use HTTPS, except that Contentful accepts HTTP on localhost for development. During in-place updates, omitting this argument retains the URL recorded in Terraform state; removing it does not clear that URL. To retain the same URL when replacing the definition, configure `src` explicitly.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `app_definition_id` (String) System ID of the app definition.
- `id` (String) Composite Terraform resource identifier in `organization_id/app_definition_id` form.

<a id="nestedatt--locations"></a>
### Nested Schema for `locations`

Required:

- `location` (String) Location identifier (e.g., entry-field, entry-sidebar, app-config).

Optional:

- `field_types` (Attributes List) Field types for which this app can be used as an `entry-field` editor. At least one definition is required. Omit for other locations. Contentful validates the configured field types and link targets. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--locations--field_types))
- `navigation_item` (Attributes) Navigation item configuration for `page` locations. Omit for other locations. When configured, both `name` and `path` must be nonempty. Omitting this object removes existing navigation item configuration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--locations--navigation_item))

<a id="nestedatt--locations--field_types"></a>
### Nested Schema for `locations.field_types`

Required:

- `type` (String) Field type (e.g., Symbol, Text, Integer, Link, Array).

Optional:

- `items` (Attributes) Required item type definition for `Array` fields. Omit for other field types. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--locations--field_types--items))
- `link_type` (String) Type of linked resource. Required for `Link` and `ResourceLink` fields; omit for other field types. For `Link`, use `Entry` or `Asset`. For linked array items, configure `items.link_type`. See [Field types](#field-types) for the ResourceLink support limitation.

<a id="nestedatt--locations--field_types--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `locations.field_types.items`

Required:

- `type` (String) Type of array items, such as `Symbol` or `Link`. Contentful validates which item types are supported.

Optional:

- `link_type` (String) Type of linked resource. Required for `Link` and `ResourceLink` items; omit for other item types. For `Link`, use `Entry` or `Asset`. See [Field types](#field-types) for the ResourceLink support limitation.



<a id="nestedatt--locations--navigation_item"></a>
### Nested Schema for `locations.navigation_item`

Required:

- `name` (String) Display name for the navigation item.
- `path` (String) Path for the navigation item, beginning with `/`, for example `/dashboard`.

### Nested Schema for `parameters`

Optional:

- `installation` (Attributes List) Parameter definitions for each app installation. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--parameters--installation))
- `instance` (Attributes List) Parameter definitions for each use of the app, such as a field editor. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--parameters--instance))

Required:

- `name` (String) Display name for the parameter.

Optional:

- `required` (Boolean) Whether the parameter is required.

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Choose one of the following methods. Match the resource address and Contentful IDs to your configuration, then review the plan before applying.

### Import by identity

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) with `identity`:

```terraform
import {
  identity = {
    organization_id   = var.contentful_organization_id
    app_definition_id = var.app_definition_id
  }
  to = contentful_app_definition.this
}
```

### Import by ID

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) with `id`:

```terraform
import {
  id = "${var.contentful_organization_id}/${var.app_definition_id}"
  to = contentful_app_definition.this
}
```

### Import with the CLI

Use the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import). Set the shell variables to your Contentful IDs before running it:

```shell
terraform import contentful_app_definition.this "$CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID/$CONTENTFUL_APP_DEFINITION_ID"
```
